title: Meet the Candidates: Krystal Adrain for Kingwood City Council | Preston County News | wvnews.com
text:
Editor’s Note: This article is part of a series of profiles on candidates for the May Primary Election. To inform voters, candidates were provided three questions relevant to their desired office; those running for the same office received the same set of questions.
Krystal Lynn Adrain, 65, is running for Kingwood City Council.
Beyond basic eligibility, what specific professional or civic experience do you possess that would make you a viable candidate for Kingwood City Council?
My education, professional experience, and love of community will make me a viable candidate for Kingwood City Council. I hold a B.S. Degree in Business Management, an A.A.S. Degree in Legal Assisting, and was a Virginia licensed title underwriter. Employed at both law firms and title/settlement companies, my career was mainly focused in the real estate field giving me the opportunity to work closely with planning, zoning, development and building departments in various ways. Past and Present Civic experiences include: 4-H Club, Pony Club, Vice President of HOA Association, The McGrew Society and the Kingwood Community Engagement Committee.
Many community members continue to cite the need for greater business growth and retention in Kingwood. As a council member, what specific tax incentives or zoning changes would you propose to attract, support and retain local businesses?
I agree there is a need for greater business growth and retention in Kingwood. One solution might be better signage, advertising, and marketing to promote local businesses and the city itself. Another possibility is to establish grants for: (1) new businesses to offset the costs of build-outs and renovations of older buildings, and (2) established businesses to offset the costs of improvements to modernize the existing facility. Concerning the zoning ordinances, the Council needs to re-visit that document and see if there are areas that need improvement or changes to make the businesses of Kingwood profitable again.
What would you say is Kingwood’s greatest need? If elected, what solutions would you propose to address this need?
I believe the greatest need is to give Kingwood’s residents and business owners a voice and a safe place to be heard. As Council Members, we are there to serve the residents and business owners of Kingwood and the needs of the Community. I’m a firm believer that there is a solution to every problem. If something isn’t working, then it’s time for a change.
